column1: # /etc/timelike/missing-commands.tsv — what a command that is not installed answers in bash (feature 007
# slice 1; spec FR-16; contract § The command-not-found answer; research R6). Read by
# One answer per line, four TAB-separated fields: name, kind, value, note ("-" for none).
#   instead  a timelike equivalent: value is the command, note says what it is
#   debian   the Debian package that provides the name: only the operator can add it (the agent has no root)
#   user     a user-level install the agent can run itself: `pip install X` lands in ~/.local, `npm install -g X`
#            in ~/.local too (the image's agent runtimes; 007 FR-26, FR-27; discovery revision 14)
# A name may have several lines, printed in file order. Every listed name must be absent from the image
# (an e2e cell checks it), and every `instead` must name an installed timelike tool (a unit test checks it).
# Names the image ships (python3, python, pip, pip3, node, npm, npx) are not listed (FR-29).
# Grows by one line per answer.
